mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% over a six-month window signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 shows two consecutive quarterly declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during episodes of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% coincident with a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6% AND PAYEMS falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS declines for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for more than three consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST surges above its 12-month MA by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% over three months signals an easing policy stance alongside falling inflation, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both < 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during episodes of both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL below 2% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of four consecutive months of PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals a sudden collapse in consumer demand, which directly reduces corporate revenues and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS falls by more than 2% month-over-month.
